cause_quote: The new shared-session cron runner took its error from `result.error`, while the handoff populated that field from delivery evidence or `Session event execution ${outcome}` without reading the operation's recorded cause.
user_saw: When a scheduled session turn failed without a detailed reply, operators saw only “Session event execution failed” in run history and the job’s last error.
summary: The fix records the operation’s failure cause when the scheduled turn has no detailed error and uses the generic message as a fallback.
reasoning: I checked the parent of #178764 and confirmed that existing custom session targets ran through the isolated cron runner, whose catch block returned the normalized exception text. The migration routed those jobs through a receipt that could fall back to generic text even when the reply operation held the original exception. The source establishes the loss of detail at that boundary, but the exact account-binding failure was only demonstrated in the fix’s evidence.
